title: Saber Responds To AI Criticisms In Rideshare Game And Promises, “We Will Never Fire Someone And Replace Them With AI”
description: One of the biggest talking points in gaming today is the use of artificial intelligence, including generative AI. It's a hot-button issue, and few companies have faced the level of criticism about it as Saber has. The developer recently found itself in hot water after CEO Matthew Karch lashed out at Rideshare Stimulator's former writer who said they were laid off and replaced by ChatGPT. Now, Saber's chief creative officer, Tim Willits, has addressed the situation as well, promising that, "We will never fire someone and replace them with AI." For anyone just catching up, Rideshare Stimulator is an upcoming Saber game where players take on the role of an Uber- or Lyft-like driver and interact with them as they take them to their location. The developers freely admit to using generative AI in various capacities, and now Willits has shed more light on the situation. He said the game's main campaign features dialogue written by humans, but there is also a "free ride" mode where Rideshare Stimulator wants to be able to reference current events in the real world. "We use AI to generate that because we want to do it so fast," Willits said, adding that the plan is for weekly or biweekly updates with this kind of AI-generated content. Willits also clarified that some of Saber's other games, including the new Hellraiser, Turok, Stuntman, and Space Marine games, also do not use AI. Saber, like many other game companies, is experimenting with AI in various ways. "We want to figure this new technology out, and we don't know exactly where it's gonna go, and our players don't know where it's gonna go, so we're all ... all of us are trying as a society to figure this out together," he said. "We want to experiment with it. I personally believe somebody [at] some game company will come up with such a brilliant idea, and we'll all be like, 'That's it.' We just need to get there." When asked specifically about claims that Saber is firing people and replacing them with AI, Willits said this is not true. "I promise you we have never let anyone go and replaced them with AI. We hire people all the time," he said. A spokesperson for Saber previously told PC Gamer that neither Saber nor Rideshare developer Unigine replaced any writers with AI for that game or any others. "In fact, Saber's staff of writers has tripled since 2023. Rideshare's story was written entirely by real people," the company said. Rideshare's "experimental, free-ride mode" does use generative AI "by necessity," Saber said, because "the number of passengers in the game is infinite." "We are firm believers in using AI tools to improve or enhance gameplay experiences and improve NPC behavior as we have done since Saber was founded in 2001. As the industry has continued to contract, Saber continues to hire. None of our 3000+ employees have to worry about being replaced by AI," the developer said. The writer in question, Stella Sacco, said Karch reached out to "apologize unreservedly" for how he spoke about Sacco. Karch had said, "Stella who? I had to ask Claude because I have never spoken to her or seen her." Sacco added in a statement that Karch said "he regretted escalating and how people online were speaking about me." "I'm not worried about being called slurs by random commenters--I'm a trans woman; that's every day for me. But it stunk to have my skill and reputation built of 20 years in games publicly maligned by someone with institutional power."

title: Hellraiser: Revival Is More Than Just Cenobites and Gore – 10 Things We Learned From Saber Interactive
description: October wouldn't feel right without a spooky game or two, and Hellraiser: Revival is shaping up to be a terrifying--and horny--dive into the nightmarish fiction of author Clive Barker. So far, the game is looking like the kind of Hellraiser experience that defined the franchise throughout the '80s and early '90s, and at Gamescom, Saber Interactive sat down with GameSpot to talk about the game, how far they're willing to go to nail the vibe of Hellraiser, and more. Hellraiser: Revival launches for PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X|S on October 6. Cliver Barker was a "permissive" partner The legendary creator of Hellraiser needed some convincing before he started collaborating with Saber Interactive, but once he was assured that the developers had a grasp of the Hellraiser franchise, he gave the studio the freedom to tell their own tale within that dark universe. "Clive Barker was such a permissive partner to work with," narrative director Anthony De Fault said. "He was really supportive of our ideas. He basically just wanted to make sure we understood Hellraiser as a franchise, and then, once he knew that we had the, we were channeling the same spirit that he was channeling back in the '80s, he just let us go." Capturing the soul of Hellraiser's greatest hits https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6Ad6CybXBC4 For the game, Saber Interactive aimed to capture the "soul" of the franchise, drawing not only from the recognizable visual elements established in the Hellraiser movies, but also from Clive Barker's original novella, The Hellbound Heart, which served as the source material for the franchise. "This game is a response, specifically to The Hellbound Heart, the first film, and Hellbound: Hellraiser 2, the second film," de Fault said. "So it's just the things that Clive was involved with that resonated really strongly with people back then. We wanted to make something that renewed that and had the same soul, but for a new medium and 40 years later." Barker was also credited as an executive producer on the third and fourth Hellraiser movies, but had no active production or creative involvement in the franchise until 2022's Hellraiser reboot. That gap saw six Hellraiser movies released, although fans usually consider this period a low point for the franchise. Saber Interactive isn't afraid of pushing ratings boards to the limits https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YCTOqk9fzO0 From what we've seen so far, Hellraiser: Revival looks like it'll be going all in on the extreme subject matter of Barker's work. Saber Interactive has confirmed that the game is going to be gory and sexy, as the studio didn't want to compromise on their vision--even if that meant it faced the risk of being denied classification in several regions. Why go that far? Because doing anything less was seen as a disservice to Hellraiser fans. "We knew what Hellraiser ought to be. We knew how disappointed Hellraiser fans would be if we did compromise, so it was just never really on the table," de Fault explained. "We wanted to pitch it at a point where I don't know if the executives would necessarily have agreed with this at the time, but we always felt like, if we get denied a rating in one or two places, we've probably done our job right. It was just important to us to do everything with purpose. All of the depraved stuff that you might encounter in the game, I think everything in there is defensible in terms of there's a reason it's there. It's not just for shock value. "It's like a good discomfort." "Comforting discomfort," Esov added. So far, it looks like the game will be available in the US, at least, as it has received an ESRB rating. It was all about execution While all of that comforting discomfort is designed with a purpose in mind, don't be too surprised if Hellraiser: Revival makes you reach for a bucket. One scene in particular might be hard to stomach, as de Fault described it as a moment of "consensual mutilation" in the game. "There's a consensual mutilation scene. In early versions of this, we failed to adequately convey to players that this was consensual. So, some people came away thinking it wasn't and that it was pretty distressing, and so we had to course-correct that. I think our intent was fully realized in the game. There wasn't really anything we wanted to do that we scaled back or anything like that. We just had to correct the execution in some places." Hellraiser: Revival takes place in the ancient year of 2006 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0rA40lqttO8 Hellraiser: Revival is set in 2006, in the small town of Claireport. Saber Interactive chose this time period as a bridge between '80s Hellraiser and the modern era, while also ensuring there wouldn't be any "super high-techy stuff" to distract players. "We still wanted it to feel like an older franchise, but just without going all the way back to the '80s," de Fault added. Pinhead has an agenda Like most Hellraiser movies, Revival revolves around a pair of sex freaks who get more than they bargained for when they use one of the infamous puzzle boxes created by the Cenobites--the all-new Genesis Configuration in this instance. Playing as Aiden, it'll be up to players to rescue his girlfriend Sunny from the Cenobites, and you can expect to run into Pinhead at several points in the story. "He plays a really substantial role," de Fault explained. He appears near the start of the game with all the other Cenobites, responding to the fact that Aiden and his girlfriend, Sunny, have used one of the configuration boxes from the game during their sexual play. In Hellraiser fashion, [the Cenobites] demand a soul, and they take somebody away who happens to be Sunny. "I probably shouldn't go further than that, but Pinhead, you encounter him multiple times. The deal that you have with him has its twists and turns, and it evolves." Pinhead is also voiced by Doug Bradley, the actor who played him in several Hellraiser movies over the decades. The "Genesis Configuration" box is fueled by suffering While previous Hellraiser media revolved around the Lament Configuration puzzle box, the Genesis Configuration is a completely new creation for the game. It serves as both a plot device and a weapon, but to use it, you'll need to fuel it with the suffering of enemies and Aiden's own anguish. Saber Interactive isn't spilling the beans on how it fits into the overall story of Hellraiser: Revival, but they did tease that it was made for a specific purpose that will be revealed eventually. "It's all in the name of this glorified violence, and basically, it gets powered by the suffering of yours and others," game director Emil Esov explained. "When there is suffering in the vicinity, you get more energy into the box, and you can perform these abilities." Cenobites can't be trusted Don't expect to be taking on iconic Cenobites in Hellraiser: Revival. They serve a variety of roles in the game, helping Aiden to unlock new powers for the Genesis Configuration or acting as unstoppable antagonists you'll have to escape. The female Cenobite--sometimes referred to as the Fallen because she was a nun who was drawn to sin in her human life--will also serve as a devil on Aiden's shoulder when she's not unlocking new powers for the Genesis Configuration. We're not worthy, we're not worthy! There's no shortage of enemies to deal with in Hellraiser: Revival, as Aiden will regularly come into conflict with the "Unworthy Ones" from the Cult of the Scarlet Church. Denied access to the Labyrinth, the worshippers of Leviathan are dangerous, but they're still fragile mortals who can be shot, skewered, and burned to death. Hellraiser: Revival's puzzles serve as a nice change of pace between all of the horror So what kind of game is Hellraiser: Revival? Esov and de Fault described as being a "puzzle-moderate" game, as when Aiden ventures into the depths of the Labyrinth, players will have solve the deadly challenges within that structure.. "There is like two to two-and-a-half hours of Labyrinth gameplay, and there is no combat in the Labyrinth," Esov said. "We intentionally designed it so the Labyrinth itself is something that is menacing, that is scary. Sometimes it's going to be, traps. Other times, it's going to be you using the Genesis Configuration to actually manipulate the Labyrinth. And then, sometimes it's the combination of the two. It's puzzle-moderate, but it's nothing like brain-crunching puzzles that require a lot of focus. "I think most of the puzzles are kind of 10-second to two-minute breathers between action or exploration sequences, that just force you to tickle your brain a little bit," De Fault added. "I'd say they occur fairly frequently, but they're not head-scratchers."

title: Gears Of War: E-Day Had To Solve One Big Lore Problem –  How Do You Get A Lancer Into The Game?
description: When Gears of War first debuted in the Xbox 360 generation, it introduced the world to the majesty of the Lancer weapon. A gun with a brutally effective chainsaw mounted to it, the Lancer has become the defining symbol of the franchise, and in Gears of War: E-Day, players will get to see just how that weapon came to be. In the established Gears of War lore, the weapon was created a year after the events of Emergence Day. That created something of a dilemma for the developer, The Coalition, as they had to give players something that reminded them of the classic weapon while telling a story that takes place during Emergence Day. The Solution? A Lancer prototype that's introduced in the game, and has roots in Gears of War literary stories. "Wherever possible, we've just done everything we can to respect the canon, right? The scene where Tai uses a chainsaw in a grocery store to kill a Locust is part of the creation story that was in a book, but we've lifted it--like all the dialogue--everything is intact in our game," creative director Matt Searcy said to GameSpot. "So even if we have to do like a small retcon, we just lift it and drop. We took the moment, we took the dialogue, we took everything about it and just said if we have to make a change, we're going to respect it as much as we possibly can, and if we need to connect the dots between two things, we're going to." https://youtu.be/SRFE0gCsgLg "We have to have a Lancer in this game. In the lore, it's created a year after E-Day by Marcus' father, so we find ways--like we revealed in our campaign preview where a prototype is built around E-Day--so we can feed into all of those things. It just takes a little bit of care and attention, and then there's usually a great creative solution to be able to respect all of the hard work that's come before and all the things the fans are deeply attached to." The book that helped inspire the story of Gears of War: E-Day is the 2008 novel Gears of War: The Aspho Fields by Karen Traviss. In it, Gear soldier Tai Kaliso uses a power saw in combat, and that action eventually goes on to inspire the creation of the chainsaw attachment for Lancer rifles. The book also covers the battle in which Dominic Santiago's brother, Carlos, dies, giving The Coalition an established starting point for building Marcus and Dom’s relationship throughout E-Day. "What it gave us was a really rich jumping-off point," Searcy explained. "So we knew E-Day is a plot point, two-thirds of the population dies, the monsters come out of the ground, and it's a cool concept. But we needed something rich for the characters to be based on, and that gave us a really strong starting point in terms of understanding where Marcus and Dom were before this game." While the story campaign has been a big focus for the early marketing of Gears of War: E-Day, we're not entirely convinced yet if it'll tell the definitive Gears story that sets up the entire franchise. The multiplayer might be where this prequel truly shines--especially with the overhauled movement systems--and you can check it all out for yourself when Gears of War: E-Day launches on October 6 for Xbox Series X|S and PC.

title: GTA 6 NPCs Will Notice If You’re Carrying A Weapon In Public
description: In Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto franchise, players have been able to walk the streets while armed to the teeth without attracting attention from the non-player characters populating the world. However, the NPCs in Grand Theft Auto 6 will be considerably more preceptive than their counterparts in the earlier games. And that means packing weapons in public is going to come at a price. According to a GTA 6 preview in The New York Times, "a player in this one cannot whip out a shotgun or a rocket launcher and walk down the street without expecting the non-player characters to call the police." As disclosed in Netflix's extended GTA 6 preview special, the game has restored the six-star Wanted level to the franchise. Presumably players will get into more trouble for firing a rocket launcher than simply holding one. But allowing the NPCs to behave more realistically to potential threats adds a new aspect that players will have to consider going forward. Although the apparent vocal stylings of the game's male antihero, Jason, have been negatively received, players have praised GTA 6's ability to interact with dogs and its potentially complex love story between Jason and his co-lead, Lucia. GameSpot has put together a comprehensive roundup of everything we learned from Netflix's GTA 6 preview. Among the highlights are the expanded map size and a Red Dead Redemption 2-like honor system that keeps track of how the players behave in the game. Grand Theft Auto 6 will be released on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.

title: Stealing Cars In GTA 6 Is Probably More Complicated Than You Expected
description: Grand Theft Auto 6 is following a tradition that Rockstar previously leaned into with Red Dead Redemption 2: a focus on realism. In the case of GTA 6, that means things like filling your car with gas, working out to get (or stay) fit, and eating to stay energized. Now we know another element of this hyper-focus: various methods for stealing cars. Whereas in past games, you could just smash the window of any car to get inside and drive off with it, in GTA 6, how you commandeer a vehicle that doesn't belong to you will be based on what kind of car it is. For older cars, you can smash the window just as you always have, but for a quieter approach, you can instead use a slim jim, a device you've maybe seen roadside assistance services use if you've ever locked yourself out of your own car. Doing it this way requires a short minigame using the control stick on your PlayStation 5 or Xbox controller. Once you get into such cars, you can hotwire them and drive off. But that's just for older cars. For newer vehicles, including whatever GTA 6's inevitable parody Tesla analog will be, you'll not be able to use these methods. Instead, you'll need a key cloner, allowing you to perform something known as a "relay attack." How you commit the crime mentioned in GTA 6's title will depend on a car's make, model, and year.These devices mimic the electronic signal that newer cars' key fobs utilize, and in both the real world and in Rockstar's satirical funhouse mirror of Florida, they allow criminals to remotely break into your car without even setting off the alarm. Presumably, this will be an item Jason and/or Lucia can keep on them as they explore Vice City, seeking all the ways to make money in GTA 6. As we learn more about this and everything else there is to know about GTA 6, you can be sure we'll bring it to you.

title: Grand Theft Auto 6 Will Have No Microtransactions Or Generative AI
description: Grand Theft Auto VI. It's the most anticipated video game of the year, and possibly of all time. Netflix just aired a 27-minute extended trailer, and you've likely read multiple stories about it right here on this site since. Multiple media outlets are now talking about recent visits to Rockstar North in Scotland, and according to one source, GTA VI won't have any microtransactions at launch, and no generative AI was used in its development. Speaking on the Kinda Funny Gamecast, Kinda Funny's Andy Cortez and Greg Miller revealed that they asked Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson about the potential for microtransactions in GTA, as well as the use of generative AI in its development. Both reported that the answer to both questions was simply "no." "Can you use your own real-world money to buy things in the game? No monetization," Cortez said. "I asked point blank, 'is AI in the game?' No AI," Miller continued. The lack of generative AI was also reported by The New York Times in its Grand Theft Auto VI feature posted earlier today. "Grand Theft Auto VI, Rockstar said, has well over 600,000 animations, compared with 55,000 animations in Grand Theft Auto V and 300,000 animations in Red Dead Redemption 2," the article said, which also confirmed that Rockstar "emphasized the new game’s human-made craft." For more on Grand Theft Auto VI, check out our coverage on just how big the map will be, whether or not you can pet (or even scold) a dog, and the return of a six-star wanted system.

title: GTA 6’s Big Netflix Extended Look: All The Things We Learned
description: After literal years of waiting since the game's official announcement, Rockstar has finally pulled back the curtain on Grand Theft Auto 6's gameplay. The Netflix-exclusive Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look gave us a chance to see the game's open-world activities, combat, story missions, characters, vehicles, and much more, which just makes the wait for November 19 even more excruciating. Below, we've rounded up our coverage so you can learn about whatever it is you're most interested in regarding GTA 6. You can pet (or scold) the dog Grand Theft Auto 6 has something for dog-lovers and dog-haters, apparently, as a button prompt showed you can not only pet dogs you come across in GTA 6, but also scold them. We would never. Six-star Wanted levels return After being absent in Grand Theft Auto 5, the six-star Wanted system returns in GTA 6. It's not entirely clear what this entails, but the crimes you've been caught committing are visible via icons under the stars. The game is long as hell No surprise here if you've played GTA 5 or Red Dead Redemption 2, but Grand Theft Auto 6 could take you a long time to complete. Rockstar North's Rob Nelson estimated his playthrough at about 80 hours, focused mostly on the main narrative and narrative-based optional content. The map is enormous Red Dead Redemption 2 featured a very large map. Grand Theft Auto 6's map is three times larger. It's not Good Theft Auto 6, after all. It's about love but Jason and Lucia don't have to be a couple The core of Grand Theft Auto 6's story is the relationship between Lucia and Jason. The two don't necessarily have to be in a romantic relationship, and can exist as platonic partners if you so choose, but the pair, together, is crucial to the story. There's a Red Dead-style Criminal Profile system Alongside the tweaked Wanted system is the Criminal Profile system. This will take into account your actions over time, like whether you choose to commit superfluous violence during your missions, and it won't be cleared back to square-one like the Wanted stars are. Jason kind of talks like Bane The guy is a little hard to understand, drawing some comparisons to Tom Hardy's Bane in The Dark Knight Rises. We're sure we'll get used to it, but we imagine Lucia has to ask him to repeat himself sometimes. The game won't directly address real-life politics Like with previous Grand Theft Auto games, GTA 6 will feature plenty of political and social satire, but it will not deal with actual, real-world political figures or events. That means no Donald Trump and no COVID-19. No microtransactions or generative AI Grand Theft Auto 6, at least the single-player game releasing in November, will not feature any microtransactions. Additionally, Rockstar says no generative AI was used in its creation.

title: GTA 6’s Jason And Lucia Aren’t Necessarily A Couple
description: GTA 6's main characters are Jason and Lucia, and while previous trailers have shown them in some steamy scenes, their relationship will be defined by how people play, not by a strict story mandate. Rockstar North's Rob Nelson confirmed to The New York Times that it will be up to the player if Jason and Lucia complete the story as a romantic couple or merely partners in crime. Players will need to manage the relationship by responding to texts and, like in any good relationship, making an effort. “It’s new for GTA, this idea of your actions having meaning in terms of how you treat your partner or how violent you are,” Nelson said. The Times report suggested that a small touch, the characters holding hands as they leave a store, is dependent on the state of their relationship. Nelson went on to say GTA 6's story will take cues from "that Bonnie and Clyde concept." He added, "We knew it was the only way for us to go with this game." Bonnie and Clyde were famous American outlaws from the early 1900s, who committed many crimes, including murder. They were lovers, and they were eventually killed by police in 1934 in Louisiana. Rockstar has also said GTA 6's story is about "whether love can survive through this storm." This was alluded to in GTA 6's first trailer. It featured the Tom Petty song "Love Is A Long Road." Petty sings about a girl he knew who “said she cared about me” but opines that “love is a long road” with many twists and turns. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. We learned a lot more about the game today, including how the map is 3X bigger than Red Dead Redemption 2's and that a playthrough can be 80 hours long. The game also brings back six-star wanted levels and that you can pet the dog.

title: GTA 6’s Jason Has A Case Of Bane-itis
description: Netflix's extended Grand Theft Auto 6 preview has arrived, and players are already dissecting the footage to glean new details about Rockstar Games' heavily anticipated sequel. So far, the response has been largely positive except in regards to the voice of Jason Duval, the game's co-leading antihero. One of the common complaints about Jason on social media is that he's difficult to understand for some listeners. This has drawn some comparison's to Tom Hardy's nearly incompressible Bane voice in trailers for The Dark Knight Rises. It's unknown if Rockstar will take any measures to adjust Jason's voice to make it easier to comprehend--as director Christopher Nolan did for Bane in the theatrical cut--but the prevailing sentiment online isn't in favor of Jason's vocals. https://twitter.com/pirate_atomsk/status/2093054631404564769 https://twitter.com/SkramDiesel82/status/2093054873608638678 https://twitter.com/MartinGriffin4/status/2093056502764277798 https://twitter.com/SilverIntoSteel/status/2093056712299143300 https://twitter.com/ricshootsraw/status/2093056133879452120 Many of the other aspects from GTA 6 have been more positively received, including the ability to interact with dogs, the return of six-star wanted levels, and more. Rockstar also recently disclosed how players can switch between controlling Jason and taking over has his literal partner-in-crime, Lucia Caminos. Prior to the new preview event, Rockstar called the recent GTA 6 leaks "heartbreaking for our team." Several years ago, Rockstar discovered the identity of a previous GTA 6 leaker and initiated legal proceedings against them. For now, the current leaker's true identity is unknown. Grand Theft Auto 6 will be released on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.

title: GTA 6 Has A Red Dead 2 Honor-Style System Tracking How Violent You Are
description: Following Grand Theft Auto 6's over-the-top Netflix gameplay reveal, Rockstar Games detailed one of the game's most important systems. Building on the traditional Wanted system from previous Grand Theft Auto titles and the Honor system from Red Dead Redemption 2, GTA 6 introduces a Criminal Profile system that tracks how violently players handle their crime sprees. The interview confirmed that the traditional Wanted system does return when you're spotted committing a crime in GTA 6. To shake off the police chasing you, Jason and Lucia may need to change vehicles and clothing, or run away and elude the police in different directions. How violent you are while committing that initial crime and escaping influences the dynamic Criminal Profile system. "This is a story about a couple on the run. We have tried to make the systems and the design support our narrative when and wherever possible," Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson told IGN. "Meaning, if you hit and run, commit a crime and run, get into trouble and move on before the cops get there, and you don’t start shooting people, don't start escalating – which you absolutely can do if you want to – but if you don’t, you’re generally going to be fine."In the same interview, it's stressed that this system isn't meant to let players make Lucia and Jason do-gooders. It's more of a tracker of how violent and maliciously players choose to commit crimes in GTA 6. Nelson says "We tried to design the game so that you have options," and that "things can escalate quite quickly if you want them to, or people who don’t want to escalate can try to avoid it." If you enjoy role-playing as a criminal in Red Dead Redemption 2 or any of GTA Online's NoPixel servers, this Criminal Profile system seems made for you. Grand Theft Auto 6 is still set to launch for PS5 and Xbox Series X on November 19, something reaffirmed by Rockstar in this gameplay reveal and its response to recent gameplay leaks.
